subtitle: Natsume · Game Boy

body: Ninja Gaiden Shadow is Natsume's Game Boy action platformer, sending Ryu Hayabusa into a threatened New York before the events of the NES trilogy. A sword, limited Fire Wheel attacks and a grappling hook provide a compact set of tools for its stages. Railings and overhead supports make the space above the character important. The player can attack while hanging, giving a dangerous section another possible route. A familiar ninja is therefore adapted through a specific set of movements rather than a direct reproduction of every ability available on the home console.

Ryu's grappling hook reaches high railings, allowing him to move beneath them and confront enemies without first returning to the floor. The level's useful positions are determined by those supports as well as ordinary platforms. Fire Wheel supplies a stronger response but has a limited stock, so saving it for the right encounter matters. The player learns when the sword and positioning are enough, and when spending a special attack can make a difficult approach safer before the next jump or climb begins.

Development began as a handheld version of Shadow of the Ninja, another Natsume action game, before becoming a Ninja Gaiden release published by Tecmo. That background helps explain its distinctive overhead movement and more concentrated toolset. Hiroyuki Iwatsuki composed the music. Released in 1991, and called Shadow Warriors in Europe, it gives the portable ninja a clear identity in motion: the hook and railings repeatedly turn the ceiling into a route, allowing the same small screen to support a fight above the obvious path.
